newsitem.title: USA: Dallas Cowboys stars cleared of sexual assault.
newsitem.headline: Dallas Cowboys stars cleared of sexual assault.

text.p: Dallas Cowboys stars Michael Irvin and Erik Williams were cleared on Friday of accusations that they sexually assaulted a woman at gunpoint, police said, after the alleged victim admitted she had lied.
Police spokesman Ed Spencer said an 11-day investigation had shown that the woman's allegations were false and that there was now no case against either Irvin or Williams.

The woman had accused Irvin of holding a gun against her head and threatening to kill her while Williams and a third, unidentified man raped her on top of a pool table inside Williams' home on Dec. 29.
She also claimed the men videotaped the assault and snorted cocaine, but the investigation failed to bring up evidence to formally charge the players with any of the allegations.

"We have determined conclusively that the allegations are not true and that a sexual assault did not take place," Spencer said. "Additionally, we have determined that Michael Irvin was not present at any time during this incident."
A police source said the woman admitted she had lied.
Irvin, 30, and Williams, 28, emphatically denied the accusations from the start. Irvin said he had not been at Williams' home in 18 months. Williams insisted he had done nothing wrong.
Spencer said the American football players had told the truth and that misdemeanor charges might now be filed against the woman. He did not say what the woman's motive was for lying.
Irvin appeared angry Friday night, telling reporters to handle the news of his innocence with the same fervor that they had reported the initial allegations.

"Rerun it, rewrite it, reprint it just like you did, with the same intensity that you did. Don't lose that intensity. Don't lose that intensity," Irvin told reporters as he got into his car after leaving the Cowboys Cafe sports bar near the team's training facility.

The two players and their attorneys have been extremely critical of the public nature of the police investigation and the media's reporting of the case. Irvin's lawyer Royce West hinted the star wide receiver might take legal action against the woman, the police or the media.
"We are tired of being a target and we are not going to take it anymore. We will in fact fight back. We have the resources to do it, and this will not go unchecked," West said at a news conference.

He compared the media frenzy in the Cowboys' case to the allegations against Richard Jewell, the guard at the Summer Olympic Games in Atlanta who discovered a bomb shortly before it exploded and then was widely named as a top suspect. He was later cleared.
"We have to look at what happened to Richard Jewell and say the same thing happened to Michael Irvin," West said.
The sexual assault allegation came after a string of ugly scandals involving sex charges, wild parties and drug abuse that rocked the Cowboys team over the last two years.
Irvin received a hero's welcome at the Cowboys Cafe sports bar near the team's training facility Friday night but declined to speak to reporters.

Irvin is currently on four years probation after pleading no contest to felony cocaine possession charges last year. If he had been arrested on aggravated sexual assault charges, he could have had his probation revoked and been sent to jail.
The Cowboys are the reigning Super Bowl champions and both Williams, a star offensive lineman, and Irvin played key roles in the club's three Super Bowl victories over the last four years.

But the team's defence of its title ended last Sunday when it was beaten in a second-round playoff game against the Carolina Panthers. Players said the commotion surrounding the assault charges played no part in the loss.
During their investigation, police searched Williams' home and took away a video recorder, several tapes, the felt from the pool table, sex toys, used condoms and other physical evidence.
The tapes showed sexual activity but police sources said there was no evidence supporting the woman's allegations that she was assaulted. Irvin did not appear on the tape.
